bug_semantics: An authenticated user with only Create permission can begin a TUS upload under an in-scope real directory, causing the default in-memory upload cache to retain the upload's absolute but only lexically resolved path for three minutes. If an ancestor directory is replaced with an escaping symlink before TTL eviction, the asynchronous raw os.Remove(item.Key()) resolves that symlinked parent and deletes an attacker-selected file outside the user's scope, bypassing ScopedFs scope checks and Delete permission.
flaw_origin: The smallest reconstructed PR member commit 99edda74cfa313d2737bcbd12ed558aa59e27e1e added ttlcache eviction to http/tus_handlers.go and first coupled an absolute file.RealPath() cache key with delayed raw os.Remove(item.Key()). It was squash-landed on the main branch by 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e. Commit 08d7a1504c42c115fdd82d3845694fe87147f1db later moved the already-vulnerable callback into http/upload_cache_memory.go while adding the Redis backend, so it is a refactor/move rather than the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object for 99edda74cfa313d2737bcbd12ed558aa59e27e1e names author Ramires Viana <59319979+ramiresviana@users.noreply.github.com> and committer Ramires Viana <59319979+ramiresviana@users.noreply.github.com>, with the complete message 'feat: track active uploads with ttlcache'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or other trailer and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-m9f5-2232-frp6 (the repository advisory for CVE-2026-73613, referenced by GHSA-px44-p4fg-h68v) documents the Create-only TUS POST, absolute RealPath registration, three-minute cache TTL, ancestor-symlink swap, raw os.Remove eviction sink, affected package metadata <=2.63.18, and patched version 2.63.19.

History search `git log --all --reverse -S 'os.Remove(item.Key())' -- http/tus_handlers.go http/upload_cache_memory.go` returned mainline squash landing 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e, move/refactor 08d7a1504c42c115fdd82d3845694fe87147f1db, and fix 9bd79c3aaeb4a55b0e69cf8976c4a258db2f5e06. The 08d7a1504c42c115fdd82d3845694fe87147f1db patch deletes the callback from http/tus_handlers.go and recreates it unchanged in new http/upload_cache_memory.go, excluding it as a BIC.

First-party PR metadata https://api.github.com/repos/filebrowser/filebrowser/pulls/5270 identifies 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e as the merge_commit_sha and reports 11 member commits. https://api.github.com/repos/filebrowser/filebrowser/pulls/5270/commits reconstructs those members; final member 40e184929ab0d8f73ed39f414942d4dfdb225427 and squash landing 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e share tree b0768b78cd59fcbb1ba36352faf6bd7bd6c13756, confirming an exact squash landing.

The decomposed BIC patch https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/99edda74cfa313d2737bcbd12ed558aa59e27e1e.patch first adds http/tus_handlers.go lines 20-39: maxUploadWait, ttlcache OnEviction, EvictionReasonExpired, raw os.Remove(item.Key()), and TTL-backed registration. The same BIC's http/tus_handlers.go lines 124-130 obtains Upload-Length and registers file.RealPath(), completing the vulnerable stored-path-to-delayed-delete mechanism.

Direct-parent tree verification used https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/76cf7bd5c2357f7950617f6ea4b5e65e8b4e8429/http/tus_handlers.go. That exact parent has only a sync.Map with Store/Load/Delete, no ttlcache import, no TTL, no eviction callback, and no os.Remove(item.Key()); therefore the vulnerable eviction lines and mechanism are absent in the BIC's immediate parent.

Release-boundary checks resolve v2.38.0 to 14b0dfec3477c57ffe89bc15675448a157e9ffe4 and v2.39.0 to e6ffb653740e37118d1882edb8d71ebe6663fece. `git diff v2.38.0 v2.39.0 -- http/tus_handlers.go` shows the callback and raw delete first appearing in v2.39.0, and `git tag --contains 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e --sort=version:refname` begins at v2.39.0. Thus the vulnerable mechanism is released in >=2.39.0, not first in v2.57.0 as the advisory narrative inferred from the later move commit.

The last-vulnerable/fixed boundary is independently confirmed: v2.63.18 resolves to fe7efb2e6afe66774cd86a5b0a03033bd514d0c0 and its http/upload_cache_memory.go tree still contains raw os.Remove(item.Key()); v2.63.19 resolves to 328f629181888760f3c8b3ff9f3b5bec50f4e54f, and `git tag --contains 9bd79c3aaeb4a55b0e69cf8976c4a258db2f5e06 --sort=version:refname` begins at v2.63.19.

Direct fix https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/9bd79c3aaeb4a55b0e69cf8976c4a258db2f5e06 removes the os import/raw delete from http/upload_cache_memory.go, stores a per-upload removal callback, invokes it on expiry (lines 47-60), and changes http/tus_handlers.go lines 112-118 to register a callback calling d.user.Fs.Remove(uploadPath), routing deletion through the uploading user's guarded ScopedFs. It also updates the Redis UploadCache implementation without introducing a filesystem delete.

reasoning: The vulnerability exists only once a Create-authorized TUS upload's absolute lexical RealPath can outlive the guarded creation operation and later reach an unguarded filesystem mutation. PR member 99edda74cfa313d2737bcbd12ed558aa59e27e1e is the smallest commit that creates exactly that lifecycle: it replaces non-expiring sync.Map tracking with a three-minute ttlcache and adds the expiry callback's raw os.Remove(item.Key()), while the existing POST supplies file.RealPath(). Its direct parent 76cf7bd5c2357f7950617f6ea4b5e65e8b4e8429 retains upload metadata indefinitely and has no eviction or raw-delete sink, proving parent absence. PR #5270 was squash-landed as 0f27c91eca581482ce4f82f6429f5dac12f8b64e; decomposing it avoids falsely treating that aggregate as the BIC. The later 08d7a1504c42c115fdd82d3845694fe87147f1db merely moves the same vulnerable callback to the new in-memory backend. Mainline/tag history places the landed mechanism in v2.39.0 through v2.63.18. Fix 9bd79c3aaeb4a55b0e69cf8976c4a258db2f5e06, first released in v2.63.19, replaces raw path deletion with a callback that calls the user's scoped filesystem Remove, so the path is guarded again at eviction time. Because the exact decomposed BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, the BIC-only attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
